subject: doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/pause-safely.md
why: New playbook, pilot 3. Steps: (1) own stop at the atomic step, children and jobs; (2) when a playbook is running, its closeout whole, with its stopped reply where one truthfully fits; (3) one wip commit, only under the owner's own words and where nothing bars it; (4) the note, keyed by the work's identity, with a frozen-tree branch; (5) own closeout. No calls, no land.

subject: cursor_plugins:playbook:pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/pause-safely
why: Map 2.22, ruling 15 and report 4.3: our stop around the Beads Pause rule, with no vendor mechanism.

modifications: No wip commit without the owner's own words covering commits on this work; the note records the uncommitted state (ruling 15). A playbook gate that commits nothing, and a frozen tree, bar it even with authority.
The note lives on the bead, or in a checkpoint file keyed by the work's identity, in the Git common directory or outside Git in the working folder.
After a refusal or partial undo the tree is frozen, tracker export included: only the checkpoint file is written, and the bead writes stay pending and named.
Pausing inside a playbook runs its closeout whole; where its contract names no fitting stopped reply, Pause states the step reached and marks proof not reached (logged, B5).
Each finished step is noted with the artifact that supports it, for Session pickup to check.
deliberately_dropped: The unconditional wip commit. revisit_when: the owner grants standing commit authority (report decision 13).

The temporary-folder resume file and the compaction trigger: a vendor mechanism, and compaction alone starts no new run. revisit_when: cr-r2pa.2.12 shows state lost across compactions, or every vendor we ship on gives a pre-compaction signal.

subject: doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/session-pickup.md
why: New playbook, pilot 3. Steps: (1) own search for the trail, delegation's explorer role when the router's rule sends a long trail to a subagent; (2) own check of the inherited state, one branch in Git and one outside it, stopping on a contradiction; (3) each proposed skip proved against its artifact, and the resume point named; (4) a verdict selecting the next unit, and how that run lists its steps; (5) read-only-closeout. Ends at its reply and changes nothing.

subject: cursor_plugins:playbook:pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/session-pickup
why: Map 2.21 and report 4.3: one pickup procedure over the existing owners, none of which changes. The session-trail contract of map row 13 is the two playbooks' own actions: reading and writing are distinct jobs that nobody asks for apart.

modifications: The trail is reused but not authoritative: consequential claims are checked before anything relies on them, and that check moves before the resume point (report 4.3).
Our trail is Beads notes, checkpoint files, what they point at and Git, with a Git branch and a no-Git branch.
A skip needs its supporting artifact opened and shown to apply to the current contents; otherwise the step is redone or the run stops.
A note authorizes nothing. The run writes nothing, tracker included, and hands on by selection, not a call.
deliberately_dropped: Cursor transcripts and cloud-agent URLs. revisit_when: an attended, workspace-scoped event record is verified.
Per-subagent reasoning level and speed: the router's delegation rule and the roster hold it. revisit_when: delegation's roster gains those fields.

subject: doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/pause-safely.md
why: Final critic, steps unchanged in number and order. The wip commit names its paths, so a path someone else staged stays staged and a file also holding another's edit stays out, and a created file is added first. The note records each path's expected state, present or deleted, and the identity is one safe filename component, checked against a file's identity line before replacing it. Closeout and reply are conditional on a note, with no note needed on the note-less exits.

subject: doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/session-pickup.md
why: Final critic, steps unchanged in number and order. Step 2 reads first and stops before any check runs; a check that may write runs only in a disposable copy or is reported unavailable. The selected work's bead trail is always reconciled with its checkpoint file, newest first, so an older bead note cannot hide a newer file. A recorded deletion is checked as absence and is not lost work.

subject: doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/pause-safely.md
why: Delta critic, steps unchanged in number and order. Two works can share a date and short name, so a matching identity line no longer proves a checkpoint is this work's: before replacing it, its bead or a stable pointer must show the same work, otherwise it is left and a distinct name taken.
